head: 339dd9f0a5c59fed2e40b550516bd50a2bf50ceb
summary: HF-008 still held. The block '# settled by SL-043' at .taad/fitness.yaml:473-501 repeated three of the twinned entries above the marker: TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags, NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core) and TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore. The copies had the same files, the same patterns and no including_comments, and one of them said the App may wait. I deleted that whole block, 30 lines including its explanatory comment, as the design's fix says. The twinned entries are stricter supersets and the App no-wait entry is unchanged. With one violation planted per rule in a temp copy, the engine's own Fitness check reported 2, 2 and 3 hits before the edit and 1, 1 and 2 after (the third file also trips a separate rule, 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore'). The full xUnit suite (400/400), rule-parity C-001 and C-003, harness C-007 and every SettledCountProbe shape all pass.

files.why: Deleted the three settled SL-043 entries and their comment block, which repeated the twinned TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags, NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core) and TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore. Every violation was reported twice, and one of the copies said the App may wait on the volume figure.

tests.note: Throwaway probe, deleted after use: it copies src and fitness.yaml to %TEMP%, plants one violation per SL-043 rule and calls taad3.fitness.check with TAAD3_HOME in scratch. Before the edit: 64 rules. EntryClassifier.cs had 2 hits (the twinned and the settled classifier rule). Scanner.cs had 2 (NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core) and 'nothing in Core waits'). VolumeSpace.cs had 3 (both ScanStore rules, plus 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore'). This reproduced HF-008's duplicate reporting.

The same plants after the edit: 61 rules. EntryClassifier.cs had 1 hit (TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags), Scanner.cs had 1 (NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core)) and VolumeSpace.cs had 2 (TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore plus the separate live-ScanStore rule). Each violation is now reported once by the SL-043 rules, and no violation appeared anywhere else.
The full default suite: 400 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. There was no machine-wide 10.0 SDK, so eng/dotnet.ps1 bootstrapped SDK 10.0.401 into the gitignored .dotnet/ first, as Q-003 decided.

Both shells printed 'rules-parity: AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 46 settled entries not compared'. The settled count is derived from the yaml, so the three deletions moved it without any edit to the test.
All checks held under powershell.exe and pwsh, and the appended-entry case read 47 settled.

Clean scenario through the engine's Fitness: CLEAN, xunit 11 Facts, 0 hits. The Fitness rule count equals twinned plus settled (61 = 15 + 46), and the 1 import rule is named NOT RUN as before. The stray-violation bite still exits 2.
All nine shapes (AppendOne to GuardRule) held under both shells, so the settled-count oracle still works on the shorter yaml.

tests.command: python.exe (taad3 venv) -c "from taad3 import fitness; fitness.check(<worktree>)" with TAAD3_HOME in a temp dir
tests.note: This is the real entry point for this change: the engine's Fitness check on the worktree itself. It reported 61 rules, 0 violations and 0 unmatched. One import rule was unran ('the provider does not use the code it checks') because it needs the engine's code graph; the verdict was 'unable' for that reason only, the same as before the edit. The App exe was not published, because this slice changes no product code.

not_built: I added no test that pins HF-008's shape, which is two fitness rules with the same files and pattern reporting the same violation twice. The design lists no cases, the fix only deletes yaml, and the minor lane says 'nothing new'. The before/after hit counts above come from a throwaway probe script in %TEMP%, which was deleted afterwards.
follow_ups: A guard (a RuleCases shape or a rules-parity check) that refuses a settled entry whose files glob and every pattern match a twinned entry, once (?m) and including_comments are normalised away. Without one, the next slice whose build twins its design's rules can bring the same duplicate reporting back.
